title: Current status of ocean observation, ensemble reanalysis and CMIP6 models in describing Antarctic Bottom Water
abstract: Abstract. Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW), a key component of the global meridional overturning circulation, forms in distinct regions around Antarctic coasts. The properties of AABW from different sources can be distinguished by their temperature and salinity properties. This study proposes a classification scheme to divide AABW into three subtypes based on their properties and geographic regions: Weddell Sea and Prydz Bay-originated AABW (WPBW), Ross Sea-originated AABW (RSBW), and Adélie Land-originated AABW (ALBW). These three subtypes are clearly identified in the World Ocean Atlas 2023 (WOA23) dataset. Taking WOA23 as a benchmark, we then systematically evaluate the ability of other datasets, including ensemble ocean reanalysis and CMIP6 models, to represent the spatial distribution and thermohaline properties of these AABW subtypes. Results indicate that the ensemble reanalysis performs well, albeit with an overestimation of ALBW. Nearly all CMIP6 models fail to capture these AABW subtypes, except after the correction of systematic temperature and salinity biases. Notably, CESM1-CAM5-SE-LR is the only model reproducing the three AABW subtypes without the correction, likely due to that the implemented overflow parameterization fits tuned physical processes. Comparison with its high resolution counterpart indicates that increased model resolution may not necessarily improve AABW simulations. This refined classification framework, along with the evaluation of various datasets, provides a foundation for more detailed investigations into the AABW formation, variability, and trends under climate change.
problem: Existing analyses often treat Antarctic Bottom Water as a uniform mass, failing to capture distinct regional subtypes, which most climate models and reanalysis datasets struggle to accurately represent due to systematic biases and inadequate representation of key formation processes.
method: This study proposes a classification scheme to divide Antarctic Bottom Water into three subtypes (WPBW, RSBW, and ALBW) based on distinct salinity ranges and a neutral density threshold, allowing for a more refined analysis of its properties from different geographic source regions.
task: The task is to classify Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) into three subtypes and systematically evaluate the ability of observational, reanalysis, and CMIP6 model datasets to represent their spatial distribution and thermohaline properties, using the WOA23 dataset as a benchmark.
innovation: This paper proposes a new classification scheme to divide Antarctic Bottom Water into three subtypes based on their origins and evaluates the performance of various ocean datasets and climate models in representing them.

This scheme is activated when the density of shelf water exceeds a predefined threshold, channeling dense shelf water through an artificial conduit directly into the deep ocean basin, thereby bypassing the explicit representation of the descent along topographic slopes. ... In this study, the models that adopt this scheme include CESM1-CAM5-SE-LR, CESM1-CAM5-SE-HR, CESM2 and FIO-ESM-2-0 (note that the remaining models do not clearly indicate the use of analogous parameterizations).
